scope: One common-dolphin record; all other 336 records and all identity/taxonomy/photo/occurrence fields unchanged

fields.before: A beaked delphinid with a dark dorsal field and a contrasting cream/gray flank hourglass. This accession follows the broad SMM common-dolphin concept; the California reference can represent a long-beaked eastern Pacific form and is not a short-beaked subspecies determination.
fields.after: A streamlined common dolphin with a distinct beak, small lateral eyes, a falcate dorsal fin and a charcoal, tan, grey and pale flank hourglass. The supplied model is reshaped and smoothly refined with original wet-skin materials. The broad SMM Delphinus delphis concept is retained; photographs do not independently settle a subspecies or regional form.

after.name: Beak, small lateral eyes and closed blowhole
after.description: Selected slim beak, low melon and small original eye surfaces. A fine closed blowhole marking sits dorsally behind the melon. Source mouth stays closed; internal airways, teeth counts and jaw mechanics are not reconstructed.

after.name: Horizontal flukes and narrow peduncle
after.description: The source flukes and caudal peduncle are smoothly refined. Posterior motion is dorsoventral, with lateral span retained. Foil dimensions, excursion and tissue mechanics are selected, without a thrust solution.

after.name: Falcate dorsal fin and flank hourglass
after.description: The dorsal fin remains a thin swept foil. Charcoal cape, warm anterior flank, grey posterior flank and pale belly form a selected common-dolphin pattern. Age, geography, lighting and individuals vary; boundaries and colour values are not calibrated.

after.name: Tapered flippers and facial band
after.description: Swept, tapered source flippers retain their connection to the torso. A fine dark band runs from the lower-jaw region toward the flipper. Shape edits and exact boundary placement are authored qualitative comparisons.
